claim:
For \(\lambda>1\), let \(R_\lambda^2=(\mathbb R^2,N_\lambda)\) be the real Banaś--Frączek plane
\[
N_\lambda(u,v)=\max\left\{\lambda|u|,\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\right\}.
\]
Its Zbăganu constant is
\[
C_Z(R_\lambda^2)=
\begin{cases}
\lambda,&1<\lambda\le\sqrt2,\\[2mm]
2\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}},&\lambda\ge\sqrt2.
\end{cases}
\]
The maximizing geometry changes sharply at \(\lambda=\sqrt2\). For \(1<\lambda<\sqrt2\), after the coordinate sign symmetries of \(N_\lambda\), exchanging the two vectors, and changing either vector sign, every maximizing pair has the form
\[
x=r\cos\alpha\,(\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha),\qquad
y=r\sin\alpha\,(-\sin\alpha,\cos\alpha),
\]
where \(r>0\) and
\[
\arccos(\lambda^{-1})\le\alpha\le\arcsin(\lambda^{-1}).
\]
At \(\lambda=\sqrt2\) this interval collapses to \(\alpha=\pi/4\). For \(\lambda>\sqrt2\), every maximizing pair is, up to the same symmetries,
\[
x=r\left(1,\sqrt{\lambda^2-1}\right),\qquad
y=r\left(-1,\sqrt{\lambda^2-1}\right),
\qquad r\ne0.
\]
Thus the low-parameter regime has a continuum of Euclidean-orthogonal extremizers, while the high-parameter regime has one transition-ray orbit whose members are not Euclidean orthogonal except at the phase point.

correctness.rationale: Writing \(N_\lambda=\max\{E,F\}\) reduces the numerator to four products. The \(EE\) and \(FF\) products are at most the denominator. For a mixed product, the quadratic minorant \(N_\lambda(z)^2\ge A_\theta z_1^2+\theta z_2^2\) gives the bound \(\lambda/\sqrt{A_\theta\theta}\). Maximizing \(A_\theta\theta=\lambda^2\theta-(\lambda^2-1)\theta^2\) over \(0\le\theta\le1\) yields \(\lambda\) below \(\sqrt2\) and \(2\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}}\) above it. Exact pairs attain both branches. Equality tracing gives the displayed complete maximizing sets.
risks: The equality classification uses only the isometries generated by coordinate sign changes, vector sign changes, and pair reversal; no coordinate-swap symmetry is assumed.
The theorem is real and two-dimensional.

value.rationale: The Banaś--Frączek plane is a classical one-parameter deformation used repeatedly to test geometric constants. The theorem gives a complete invariant phase diagram, not an isolated value: the sharp constant changes formula exactly at \(\lambda=\sqrt2\), and the extremal set simultaneously changes from a continuum of Euclidean-orthogonal pairs to a single transition-ray orbit. This identifies which part of the strip--disk geometry controls Zbăganu distortion in each regime and supplies a natural benchmark for comparisons among Ptolemy, von Neumann--Jordan, and Zbăganu constants.
risks: The result is a two-dimensional model-family theorem rather than a general Banach-space bound.
